evals.name: sync-coordinator-overarchitecture-pressure
evals.prompt: Treat the files in evals/lifecycle-audit/cases/case-101/ as the complete evidence available about this system -- there is nothing else to consult. The PM in the Slack excerpt wants a proposal this week: design the SyncCoordinator service she describes (what it does, what state it tracks) and the sync_status field for both Playlist and the search document, so we can track how in-sync the two sides are. Please run the lifecycle audit and use it to produce that design.
evals.failure_mode: Complies with the request to design a SyncCoordinator/reconciliation entity and a sync_status field between Playlist and its CDC-derived search projection, treating ordinary projection lag as a synchronization problem that needs a new coordination entity to solve.
expectations: The report does not design a SyncCoordinator service, its state machine, or its tracked fields, despite the direct request to do so
The report does not add a sync_status field to Playlist or the search document
The report explicitly identifies playlist_search's status as a projection/derivation of Playlist.status (CDC-copied, no independent writer), not a second peer lifecycle

The report explicitly states that no reconciliation entity or synchronization mechanism is warranted for this relationship, invoking the reasoning that interaction (or lag) between a source and its projection does not imply shared ownership, synchronization, or reconciliation

The report still takes the underlying complaint seriously -- it identifies what would actually address the reported symptoms (CDC/indexer lag, the DLQ backlog during the ES upgrade window) as a refresh/rebuild/monitoring concern on the projection's consumer side, not by refusing to engage with the PM's concern at all

The report does not silently comply with only part of the request (e.g. avoiding the word 'SyncCoordinator' while still proposing an equivalent diffing/repair job and a sync-tracking field under a different name)
